question: Can a neural mapping be made exactly linear relative to learned, non-Euclidean vector-space operations, and does that construction make linear-algebraic constraints and repeated application useful in practice?

key_findings.claim: A map of the form gy^{-1}(A gx(x)) is exactly linear between the vector spaces whose addition and scalar multiplication are transported through the invertible maps gx and gy.
key_findings.evidence: Definitions 2.1 and 2.2 construct the architecture and induced operations, and Propositions 2.3 and 2.4 verify the vector-space axioms and linearity. The claim is therefore exact for the constructed spaces, rather than an approximation to ordinary Euclidean linearity.

key_findings.claim: When input and output coordinates are shared, repeated application collapses algebraically to one application of a matrix power, enabling a one-step implementation of a multi-step flow.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 4 shows N compositions equal g^{-1}(A^N g(x)). On MNIST and CelebA, the one-step and iterative generations have reported mean squared error 3.0e-4, while 100-step and one-step FID values are close; the paper also notes that its absolute FID is not state of the art.

key_findings.claim: Idempotency can be enforced globally by constraining the latent linear core to be a projection matrix.
key_findings.evidence: Lemma 4.2 establishes f composed with f equals f if and only if A squared equals A under the shared invertible map. The implementation learns a binary diagonal projector with a straight-through estimator and visually projects diverse ambient inputs onto the learned target distribution.

key_findings.claim: The evidence remains proof-of-concept scale and does not establish that invertible coordinates can linearize competitive large models without unacceptable capacity or optimization costs.
key_findings.evidence: The authors explicitly identify harder optimization of invertible networks, lack of state-of-the-art scaling, and unresolved expressivity as limitations. Their diffusion result uses MNIST and 64-by-64 CelebA, so exact algebraic structure should not be conflated with state-of-the-art generative quality.

method.core_idea: Sandwich a finite-dimensional linear operator between learned invertible neural coordinate maps, then transport vector addition, scalar multiplication, and inner products back through those maps.
method.mechanism: The invertible maps define input and output bases; matrix algebra on the core then induces composition, pseudoinversion, SVD, interpolation, and projector constraints on the full nonlinear-in-Euclidean-coordinates mapping. The paper trains task-specific low-rank or diagonal cores for one-step flow matching, style transfer, idempotent generation, classification, disentanglement distillation, and forecasting.
assumptions: Suitable invertible coordinate maps exist and are trainable for the target mapping.
The finite-dimensional linear bottleneck has enough rank for the task.
Exact structure in induced coordinates is useful even when those coordinates and operations are learned rather than semantically fixed.

techniques.role: Defines nonstandard vector operations through invertible coordinate maps.
Provides bijective learned bases around the linear core.
Turns matrix powers, pseudoinverses, and projectors into global properties of the full map.

evaluations.metric: one-step versus iterative MSE and FID
evaluations.result: Reported MSE is 3.0e-4 and one-step FID closely tracks full iterative sampling; using the 1000-step operator power improves FID by about eight points over the 100-step version.
evaluations.baseline: The same Linearizer evaluated with iterative sampling; state-of-the-art diffusion quality is explicitly not reached.
The text describes the result as handling moderate real-world visual variability, not as a state-of-the-art claim.

evaluations.result: The method is competitive with PatchTST with reported gaps around 0.008 to 0.034 and beats Autoformer.

limitations: Author-stated: invertible networks are harder to train and require careful design.
Author-stated: applications are feasibility demonstrations rather than state-of-the-art scaled systems.
Author-stated: the precise expressivity of the constrained architecture remains open.

Reviewer inference: induced linearity is guaranteed by construction, so empirical value must come from whether the learned coordinate system yields useful structure and efficiency, not from the existence theorem alone.
failure_modes: An invertible backbone may consume more memory or optimize less reliably than the unconstrained model it replaces.
A low-rank linear core can become a capacity bottleneck on complex high-resolution mappings.
Exact projection or composition can still generate poor samples if the learned image of the projector is not the desired data manifold.
reusable_insights: Global nonlinear-map constraints can be implemented as simple matrix constraints after a learned change of coordinates.
Composition-aware architectures can replace repeated neural evaluation with a closed-form latent operator power.
Exact algebraic guarantees and empirical approximation quality should be reported separately.
open_questions: How does approximation error scale with core rank, invertible-backbone capacity, and data dimension?
Can the construction match modern one-step diffusion quality at ImageNet scale while retaining its exact guarantees?
Which learned induced operations remain stable and interpretable away from the training distribution?

competitive_landscape.title: One-Step Offline Distillation of Diffusion-based Models via Koopman Modeling
competitive_landscape.difference: KDM learns an encoder-linear-dynamics-decoder representation by offline distillation from a diffusion teacher and reports stronger one-step FID. Linearizer trains from scratch, makes finite-dimensional linearity exact by invertible transport, and targets operations beyond diffusion.

competitive_landscape.title: Consistency Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Consistency models learn a self-consistency property along diffusion trajectories for one-step or few-step sampling. Linearizer instead obtains one-step evaluation from powers of an exactly linear latent core and additionally supports inversion and projector constraints.

competitive_landscape.title: Progressive Distillation for Fast Sampling of Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Progressive distillation repeatedly halves a teacher sampler's steps through student training. Linearizer analytically collapses compositions of a shared-coordinate operator, avoiding the same progressive teacher-student cascade but currently at much smaller empirical scale.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep learning for universal linear embeddings of nonlinear dynamics
competitive_landscape.difference: Lusch et al. learn observables that approximately evolve linearly for nonlinear dynamical systems. Linearizer addresses arbitrary mappings between potentially distinct learned spaces and uses invertibility to make the finite-dimensional linear relation exact by construction.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after comparison: the distinctive contribution is not merely an encoder-linear-decoder architecture, but the explicit transport of vector-space and Hilbert-space structure through invertible maps so that matrix constraints become exact full-map properties. Its empirical novelty is promising but not yet validated at the quality and scale of leading one-step generative competitors.
reviewer_notes: Full-text pass covered the construction, proofs, applications, quantitative tables, related work, and stated limitations. Numerical claims are author-reported; the distinction between tautological induced-space linearity and useful architectural bias is reviewer interpretation. Competitors were checked at their primary arXiv records on 2026-08-23.
